messages.subject: Re: memory problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gilbert,

Thanks for this reproducible example.  The problem has to do with a step of internal processing where the case of very high numbers of edges (relationships between nodes) explodes the size of an R object used in the processing.  I believe I have it fixed, but I’ll have to ask you to install from a github branch to try it.  There is a subsequent processing issue raised by your example that I’m also fixing.  I’ll let you know when I have something ready for you to try.  In addition there are ways your model can be written more compactly in nimble that I will send along.  I just wanted to give you an update for the moment.

Perry

messages.subject: Re: memory problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gilbert,

I think if you can install from our devel branch on github it will do better.  You can do that by

library(devtools)
install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")
(unfortunately that seems to install some packages that are suggests but not imports).
Your model is still large due to all the latent occupancy states, so the building will still be slow.  In the attached file I’ve shown some steps you can take to improve it by vectorizing some declarations and using a user-defined distribution to avoid some of the BUGS code constructions you had.  One could go further and use more effective samplers for the z[i,j] latent states or cut them completely out of the model by writing a user-defined distribution that directly sums over them.  User-defined functions and distributions are in section 5.2.5 of the user manual.  Let us know if we can support you in that.

Perry
